absent: Bit definitions and combination rules for idle balance kick requests
Memory ordering and lifetime guarantees for atomic flag and per processor helpers
Delivery and execution guarantees for cross processor calls and deferred idle balancing
Ownership and synchronization of shared domain busy counters
Initial values and wrap handling for load timing and frequency parameters
Hierarchy and enablement rules for pressure groups and polling work
Contracts for class level balancing and tick handling including retry signalling
Eligibility and slice protection rules for deadline scheduling
Enablement and occupation accounting for core scheduling and forced idle
Selection rules for housekeeping processors and workqueue timing guarantees

findings.text: Idle exit hook is globally visible and applies to the local run queue, clearing its stopped tick marker and withdrawing the processor from the shared idle set while marking the last level cache domain busy when such domain state exists.

Periodic load tick and folding helpers expose the interface that merges per queue runnable and uninterruptible counts into a global delta, emitting a contribution only when the locally cached active total changes.

Interrupt time accounting for pressure stall information is globally visible and attributes elapsed device time to the incoming group hierarchy, with early dismissal for disabled infrastructure, idle tasks, unchanged groups and non positive elapsed intervals.
Preemption depth adjusters are globally visible entry points that change the nesting count and invoke latency tracing hooks at the transition boundaries.

Fair class selection helpers are globally visible and choose among queued deadline entities, delegating delayed entities to sleep handling and consulting idle balancing when the local hierarchy appears empty.
Core scheduling force idle accounting forms a visible chain from periodic tick through per core aggregation to per task and per cgroup charging.
Tick offload initialization is a boot time entry point that allocates per processor control storage and treats allocation failure as fatal.
Remote nohz load folding is a visible helper that forwards a remote queue to the shared folding path for inclusion in the alternate buffer.

Idle balancer target selection prefers a processor whose whole sibling group is idle, remembers the first idle processor as fallback, narrows the candidate set when encountering busy or partially idle groups, and reuses a per processor scratch mask.

Idle balancer kicking advances the global balance deadline for full requests, skips targets that already carry all requested work, and grants ownership of the shared call data to the setter of the first flag.
Deadline entity choice respects singleton identity, cached buddy eligibility, current slice protection and deadline ordering under eligibility filtering with comparison against the current entity.
No tick load index selection observes the published update point under ordering guarantees and moves to the alternate buffer once the folding window has begun.

Several configuration variants collapse scheduling hooks to empty operations, including idle balancer kicking, frequency tick scaling, core tick handling, pressure accounting shims, remote tick control, latency hooks and statistic increments.
Class traversal helpers iterate over the active scheduling hierarchy either across the full span from highest to lowest or across a caller supplied subrange ending before the idle class.
Tree node conversion yields the enclosing deadline entity and deadline comparison orders entities by their deadline values.
Hardware load averaging hook in this configuration constantly reports no contribution regardless of time or capacity inputs.
Extended scheduler switch predicate has two build dependent forms, one consulting a rarely taken branch indicator and one constantly reporting false.
Target selection for idle balancing requires disabled interrupts to protect reuse of the local selection mask.
Pressure interrupt accounting and core force idle aggregation require ownership of the associated run queue, with pressure updates additionally bracketed by per processor write sequencing.
Remote tick handling serializes against local scheduling with run queue locking under disabled interrupts, while offload lifecycle and idle flag ownership rely on atomic state manipulation.
Remote tick control combines a processor identifier with an atomic lifecycle marker and a deferred work item for periodic execution.
Remote tick lifecycle values are zero for offline, one for offlining and two for running.

Offload control moves from offline to running on start with an initial delayed queue, remains running with periodic requeue about once per second, and moves to offlining on stop without cancellation so the handler observes the transition.
Fair idle handling distinguishes retry signalling from fresh work discovery and from persistent emptiness, rescanning on new arrivals and propagating retry upward.

Remote tick work handler runs in process context and performs scheduler tick work only for online processors whose local tick appears stopped, covering clock maintenance, class tick handling and load folding.
Next task selection combines a narrow fair only fast path with a general balancing pass plus ordered class walk supporting restart and guaranteed idle fallback.

Scheduling debug checks detect corrupted task stack boundaries, sleeping inside non blocking sections, entry under atomic context and entry from user context, with atomic entry producing a diagnostic report and taint.
Preemption depth updates include debug checks for negative counts, mismatched decrements and imminent overflow of the spinlock portion.
Force idle aggregation discards empty start markers and non positive elapsed intervals and warns when occupation accounting is missing despite forced idle presence.
Processor time charging updates the local root cell before delegating to hierarchical group accounting, ensuring the common case is handled first.
Core tick wrapper triggers detailed force idle handling only when core scheduling is active for the queue and statistic collection is enabled.
Enabled statistic macro increments the supplied counter while the disabled variant discards the operation.
Preemption latency hooks emit tracing events when the nesting depth equals the boundary value on entry and exit, capturing the caller context for offline analysis.
